domains.heading: Start with the participant
domains.summary: A subject-level view gives observations a common identity, rather than repeating background attributes in every measurement row.
domains.recordGranularityExplanation: One subject in the teaching extract. This is a useful join anchor, not a complete submission definition.
domains.explanation: Imagine two app databases both assign participant number 001. A stable study-aware identity prevents a join from attaching one person's observations to another. Keep local application keys separate from exported identifiers.
domains.pitfall: Treating a demographic row as a mutable master record can erase the meaning of an earlier extract. Preserve the extraction context and document changes.

sourceRefs.claimScope: Conceptual education; not copied normative metadata
Teaching context only

domains.heading: Follow an occurrence over time
domains.summary: Event data describes something that happened, with dates that may have different precision and an account of what was reported.
domains.recordGranularityExplanation: One fictional reported event per row; multiple rows can belong to one subject.
domains.explanation: An event may begin in a known month but lack an exact day. Preserve that uncertainty instead of forcing it through a date-picker default. The identity of an event is separate from its position in a sorted table.
domains.pitfall: A severity description does not determine seriousness. Neither a UI color nor symptom wording can safely derive a clinical classification.

sourceRefs.claimScope: Conceptual education; not copied normative metadata
Teaching context only

domains.heading: Describe treatment alongside a study
domains.summary: Medication records help describe treatment occurring around a study without assuming it is the study intervention itself.
domains.recordGranularityExplanation: One authored treatment record in this lesson; real record granularity needs the applicable guide and study specification.
domains.explanation: A participant may report a treatment name and a partial start date. Store the original report and its provenance before attempting standardization. A product identifier in an application is not automatically an approved dictionary code.
domains.pitfall: Do not join medications by display name or infer a controlled drug code from free text. Repeated courses may need distinct identities even when their names match.

sourceRefs.claimScope: Conceptual education; not copied normative metadata
Teaching context only

domains.heading: Separate a plan from an administration
domains.summary: Exposure lessons focus on treatment represented in the study data rather than what a scheduling screen says should occur.
domains.recordGranularityExplanation: One illustrative treatment exposure record, not a complete dosing history.
domains.explanation: A planned dose is an instruction; an observed administration is evidence of an action. A system that treats a scheduled item as a completed event can manufacture exposure. Keep the two states distinct before considering any tabulation.
domains.pitfall: A dose number alone has no unit, route or timing context. Our short lesson deliberately does not claim that EXDOSE is enough to describe an administration.

sourceRefs.claimScope: Conceptual education; not copied normative metadata
Teaching context only

domains.heading: Keep a result with its context
domains.summary: A laboratory value is only interpretable with its test identity, unit, collection context and representation.
domains.recordGranularityExplanation: One test result per row in the teaching model; it is not one row per laboratory panel.
domains.explanation: A form may present several results in adjacent cells. A findings-oriented representation can instead put each result on its own row. Keeping the original result as text preserves qualifiers that a numeric database column would discard.
domains.pitfall: Do not strip comparison symbols or silently convert units. Neither the selected variables nor the illustrative values provide a clinical interpretation or a full laboratory mapping.

sourceRefs.claimScope: Conceptual education; not copied normative metadata
Teaching context only

domains.heading: Turn measurements into observations
domains.summary: Repeated measurements make the difference between a collection form and an observation table visible.
domains.recordGranularityExplanation: One fictional measurement per subject per row; our example contains two measurements for each of two subjects.
domains.explanation: A single encounter object can contain several measurements. Flattening it into one wide record hides the repeating measurement structure. Follow the input observation ID through the mapping manifest to see which source observation produced each output row.
domains.pitfall: Do not call a made-up measurement token official terminology. The walkthrough uses explicit teaching tokens and never claims a submission-ready dataset.
